mainEntity.name: Is it better to build a new addition or convert an existing garage?

acceptedAnswer.text: A garage conversion repurposes enclosed, existing square footage under a shared roof, whereas a ground-up room addition requires pouring a new foundation, framing exterior walls, and constructing a new roofline. Converting a garage is typically faster and does not encroach on yard setbacks, but you permanently lose covered vehicle parking and vehicle-related storage. A ground-up addition lets you design the layout, ceiling height, and window placement from scratch without compromising your garage, though it involves higher structural, foundation, and roof tie-in labor.
acceptedAnswer.description: A garage conversion reuses existing structural walls but eliminates parking, while a new addition preserves storage and provides complete freedom over room dimensions.
